sections.h2: Which Rome offices bill and value Floyd County property?
sections.html:
In Floyd County one office sets values and another collects, and both work out of Rome. The Tax Commissioner is in the Floyd County Historic Courthouse at 5 Government Plaza, Suite 109, Rome, GA 30161, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 26, Rome, GA 30162. For property tax, call (706) 291-5146 or (706) 291-5148 on weekdays between eight and five.

The assessors appraise every real and personal property account in the county and in Rome itself. The Assessor's Office moved to the former Law Enforcement Center at 5 Government Plaza, and its phone is (706) 291-5143.

Tax for the City of Rome is on the county bill. The three rate-setters are the Floyd County Board of Commissioners, the Rome City Commission and the Floyd County Board of Education.

sections.h2: Floyd County homes and who owns them
sections.html:
Floyd spreads across 509.81 land square miles, and about 101,378 people lived here in mid-2025. Renters hold a large slice: owners occupy 63.6 percent of homes. A typical owned home is valued at $217,900 and median gross rent is $1,014 a month. The county counts 41,737 housing units and 36,856 households, and issued 330 building permits in 2025. With values near $218,000 and rents just over $1,000, the tax questions below matter to landlords and families selling a parent's house as much as to owner-occupants.

A house in town and a house outside it go through the same assessors but can carry different bills, since the city rate applies only inside Rome. Ask which taxing districts cover your parcel.

The usual due date is November 15, with real and personal property statements mailed by September 1.

  • Interest builds monthly once the date passes, and a late penalty reaching 20 percent can be added.
  • Mobile homes get statements by February 1 and owe by April 1; a late payer faces a 10 percent penalty and possibly a citation.
  • For mailed checks the office honors a U.S. Postal Service postmark and rejects metered ones.
  • The office mails to the owner and never to the lender, so pass your copy along if a servicer pays your tax.
  • A bill left open more than 90 days can be answered with a tax fifa, a lien recorded at the Clerk of Superior Court where credit bureaus can read it.

Floyd County holds tax sales in the spring, with listings posted on the Tax Commissioner's website. Ask the office when the next sale schedule is published.

sections.h2: What a Floyd County assessment notice shows
sections.html:
The notice states the current value of the parcel and the estimated millage rates certified by each taxing jurisdiction. The estimated tax on it cannot be the basis for an appeal, since only the value, taxability or uniformity can be argued.

The notice lists four ways to file, and you pick one and must also state a valid opinion of value. Notices returned as undeliverable are posted on a list under Georgia code section 48-5-306(c). Each listed property gets 30 days from the posting date to appeal, and the assessors do not extend that time for an owner who failed to check the list. Anyone who moved, inherited a parcel or changed a mailing address should call the assessors at (706) 291-5143 and confirm the record, so a missed notice does not cost the appeal.

sections.h2: How to challenge your Floyd County value
sections.html:
Send a written appeal to the Floyd County Board of Assessors, 5 Government Plaza, Rome, GA 30161, within a 45-day window that starts on the notice date. One that arrives or is postmarked after the deadline does not count.

Steps after a Floyd County notice of assessment
StepWhat happensTime limit
Written appealFiled with the Board of Assessors along with your own opinion of value45-day window from the notice date
Staff reviewAppraisers raise, lower or keep the value30 days to contest a changed value
Board of EqualizationA three-person panel named by the Grand Jury, serving three-year terms, hears the caseCertified automatically when the value is unchanged
Superior CourtOpen to either side after the board rulesWritten notice to the Board of Assessors

Arbitration is available instead of the Board of Equalization, at the owner's option when the appeal is filed. Grounds are taxability, uniformity, value and denial of homestead. Your letter should carry the map reference from the notice, your chosen method, your estimate of what the value should be, a short reason and a daytime phone number.

Local Floyd exemptions replace the state ones wherever the local amount is bigger. Regular, veteran and elderly homestead exemptions are offered, with an extra exemption at age 62. Go to the Tax Assessor's Office, and carry the warranty deed if this is your first home.

A form can arrive any month, yet an application received after April 1 starts the benefit a year later. After approval it renews on its own until the residence, owner or exemption type changes.

  • A building listed on the Georgia register of historic places may earn preferential assessment, covering the structure, its land and up to two acres around it.
  • Bona fide farm use qualifies for assessment at 30 percent, and conservation use programs ask for a covenant of at least a decade.
  • Timber still standing escapes tax until cut or sold.
  • Manufacturers may qualify for freeport exemption, with applications taken during the return season that ends April 1.

Before signing a contract on land under such a covenant, ask the assessors what the sale does to it.

sections.h2: Selling with the tax bill in mind
sections.html:
Request the balance from the Tax Commissioner and write the year's split into the contract. Values are fixed as of each January 1 and statements generally follow by September 1, so a spring sale can close before the year's bill exists.

The Floyd County Clerk of Superior Court, not the tax office, collects intangible tax on a long-term mortgage, and warranty deed copies come from its deed room at 3 Government Plaza. A mobile home seller should confirm the April 1 tax and decal are current.

Assessment notices are also tied to site visits. The assessors must notify owners before inspecting, as Georgia code section 48-5-264.1 directs, and visits follow a sale or purchase, new construction, an active building permit, a return, an appeal or an exemption application. Appraisers drive marked county vehicles and carry identification.

When a buyer pays cash, there is no lender appraisal and no loan underwriting, so the closing date depends on your paperwork. The tax steps stay the same: get the commissioner's balance, settle older years from proceeds, and agree in the contract on the current bill. For a rental or an inherited house, a fast closing also ends the cycle of monthly interest on a late account.

faqs.q: When are Floyd County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Houses, land and business equipment usually come due November 15, while mobile homes come due April 1.

faqs.q: What is the Floyd County appeal window?
faqs.a: Appeals are written and due within the 45-day window, at 5 Government Plaza in Rome. Late ones are rejected.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Floyd County property tax?
faqs.a: Interest accrues monthly after November 15 and a penalty that can reach 20 percent may follow. Continued nonpayment can bring a lien and further collection steps.

faqs.q: Does the City of Rome send its own property tax bill?
faqs.a: No. Taxes for the City of Rome are included on the Floyd County tax bill. The county commissioners, the Rome City Commission and the Board of Education each set their own rate.

faqs.q: Where do I get a copy of my Floyd County warranty deed?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Superior Court's deed room, in the new Floyd County Courthouse at 3 Government Plaza in Rome, supplies copies of a warranty deed.
